# Bosonic Noise Dimension

The project studies one-mode iid random Weyl displacement channels. The noise law is known, every draw is hidden and the noise second moment is finite. The input resource is the unconditional mean photon budget per use, averaged over the block and over any adaptive history. For E at least one, the same formula estimates ordinary and adaptive two-way-assisted quantum capacity to bounded additive error. Subtract the Shannon entropy of square-bin quantization of the noise at resolution 1/sqrt(E+1) from log2(E+1). The upper error depends only on a second-moment bound, and the lower error is universal.

## Scientific distinctions to preserve

Thermal coherent information is an achievable ordinary-rate lower bound. The adaptive converse applies to arbitrary local operations and two-way classical communication, with no free preshared entanglement. The two capacities lie within a bounded gap of one another. Random displacement operators generally do not commute, although their random-unitary channels compose by classical convolution. Information dimension measures the growth of the quantized entropy as the bins shrink.

At information dimension two the logarithmic energy coefficient vanishes. The explicit bounded-support density nevertheless gives triple-logarithmic growth. Finite Gaussian-relative entropy supplies the exact boundedness criterion under the noise-moment hypothesis. For independent Gaussian jitter of variance b, the broadening law uses the effective resolution (b + 1/(E+1))^(-1/2). Fixed positive jitter gives a finite ceiling. The capacity definition takes the blocklength to infinity at fixed channel parameters and energy.

The proofs establish unrestricted asymptotic rates with bounded additive errors. The constants need not coincide at the lower and upper endpoints. The phase-noise antecedent supplies the shared entropy-resolution principle. Weyl displacements have a different error algebra, relevant resolution and converse.

The cyclic-phase comparison is a separate composed-channel result. At mean energy eJ and displacement variance beta/J, the displacement-only quantum capacities grow as log2(J)+O(1). Adding a J-point cyclic phase twirl makes the limiting quantum, two-way entanglement and two-way key capacities finite and equal. The environment within each net shift has a coherent loss-and-gain vector. An artificial channel with only a shift record and identical Fock transitions has a strictly greater optimized limiting rate at positive e and beta.
